functionality.rationale: The task is the first production composition that must drive pairing, offers, transfer progress, commit, rejection, and cancellation between real processes.

security.rationale: Unauthenticated dispatch, peer-controlled paths, premature commit, or incorrect transport binding could expose or overwrite local files.

performance.rationale: Partial socket I/O, frame queues, file workers, and progress publication must remain bounded for large one-file transfers.

compatibility.rationale: The implementation must preserve the accepted C ABI and protocol v1 while replacing fail-closed production backends.

concurrency.rationale: Socket callbacks, ordered publication, ACK completion, cancellation, file workers, and shutdown race across engine-owned executors.

platform.rationale: Socket behavior, file opening, receive-root handling, atomic commit, and worker teardown vary across supported desktops.

persistence.rationale: Accepted files must commit atomically while rejection, cancellation, integrity failure, and process exit leave no durable partial artifact.

adr.rationale: ADR 0008 and the accepted protocol and security ADRs already define the production backend boundary implemented here.

architecture.rationale: The task fills existing core, bridge, session, transfer, and storage composition without changing dependency direction.

roadmap.rationale: XT-032 closes the vertical-slice roadmap only after packaged cross-platform evidence.
